name: The Met High School Internship Program (Summer)
what_you_do: Work 40 hours over the summer in a Met department such as curatorial, social media, education, imaging or design. You meet museum staff, join a cohort, and go to Teen Fridays. No art background needed.
grades: 10th or 11th grade, or working on a High School Equivalency
who_can_apply: Students in grade 10 or 11 (or getting a High School Equivalency) who live in and attend a high school or home school in New York, New Jersey, or Connecticut. You need working papers, a Social Security Number or ITIN, a parent or guardian's consent, and must not have done another Met internship.
pay_detail: $1,100 stipend when you finish, which the page says matches New York State minimum wage law.
duration: 40 hours, about 10 to 20 hours a week. In 2026: bootcamp July 1, placement July 7 to Aug 7, plus a June 27 family reception.
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was Friday, March 13, 2026, 5 pm ET, with interview notices by mid-April. 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Online application form, short essays, and one letter of recommendation from an adult who is not related to you. Finalists do an in-person group interview.
notes: All listed dates are mandatory, and a parent or guardian must come to the reception. The Met also runs a spring semester internship for New York City students only. Connecticut is not a region on this site yet, but Connecticut students can apply.
